acceptance: Two configs differing only in nested key order produce the same database name.
Names for configs without nested dicts are unchanged (golden test) or a documented migration is provided.
Callers listed in the description are covered by tests.
context: Defect found during the Spark tuning review (2026-09-30), requested as its own item by the user. Not a prerequisite for the Spark tuning items.
description: benchbox/utils/database_naming.py ~L206 builds the tuning hash from str(sorted(config_copy.items())), which sorts only top-level keys, so reordering a nested dict (e.g. a platform_optimizations map) changes the generated database name. The hash is md5 truncated to 6 characters. Production callers exist: build_adapter_config (benchbox/platforms/base/config_utils.py ~L239) when no database name is given, plus bigquery.py ~L198 and databricks/adapter.py ~L497. An earlier note that "Spark does not use hash naming" was not established; check which Spark-family adapters reach it through build_adapter_config. Fix with canonical JSON (recursive sort_keys) and decide, with the user, how to handle existing names: changing the digest renames databases for configs that contain nested dicts, so either keep the old digest for configs without nested dicts or provide a migration note. Until fixed, new nested maps (such as the spark tuning map) should be sorted when parsed, which spark-session-config-model already requires.
